articles.author: trenton
articles.description:
We like to believe that once something disappears from our screen, it disappears from the internet.
It doesn’t.
Every location check-in, every photo upload, every comment on a forum leaves behind small fragments of information. Individually they may look harmless, but when stitched together they form a surprisingly detailed story.
Over the past few months, while digging into open-source intelligence (OSINT), I realized how easy it is to reconstruct someone's online presence just by following these breadcrumbs. A geotagged photo here, a reused username there, and suddenly you have a trail spanning multiple platforms.
For example, imagine someone using the username Dry_Board7594 across different platforms. It might appear on a photo-sharing site, a developer forum, and a microblogging platform. Individually they seem unrelated, but together they start forming a map of that person's digital footprint.
Most people think privacy leaks happen through hacks or data breaches. In reality, many of them happen through information we willingly share.
A picture taken at a cafe can reveal the location.
The internet never truly forgets.
So the next time you upload something, ask yourself one question:
What story would someone be able to build from the pieces you leave behind?
articles.title: Title: Digital Footprints: How Much Do We Really Leave Behind?

articles.author: The Pragamatic Architect
articles.description:
Most developers think deploying an LLM is the product. It's not. It's just the beginning.
An LLM can generate text, summarize documents, and answer questions — but real enterprise applications need far more:
➡️ Accessing live data sources
➡️ Calling external APIs
➡️ Executing multi-step workflows
➡️ Integrating with enterprise systems
This is where LangChain comes in. LangChain is the orchestration layer that transforms a raw LLM into a real, production-grade application.
At its heart, LangChain executes tasks step by step in a linear pipeline. Each step receives the output of the previous one.
Input → Retrieve Data → Build Prompt → Call LLM → Output

This is why it's called LangChain — it literally chains operations together. Every stage runs in order. That determinism is exactly what ent…
articles.title: Building LLM Apps Using LangChain AI Orchestration

Persistent — a running service with stable endpoints, not a script I run manually
Modular — add new sites without touching the core codebase
AI-ready — expose scraped data as tools that language models can call

articles.description:
I built a multiplayer Wordle where you win real SOL - here's how


A few weeks ago I had a simple idea: what if Wordle had real money on the line?
The result is WordGuess - a multiplayer word game on Solana mainnet. Every 2 minutes, a new 7-letter word is chosen. Players pay 0.01 SOL per guess. First to guess correctly wins 95% of the prize pool. Fully automated, no custodial wallets, no signups.
Here's how I built it and what I learned.
Next.js — frontend, deployed on Vercel
Supabase — PostgreSQL + Edge Functions + Realtime
Solana mainnet — payments and payouts via Helius RPC
Phantom / Solflare — wallet connection
The core idea: keep the game logic server-side (so the secret word is never exposed), but make payments fully on-chain.
A cron job runs every minute and checks if there's an act…
articles.title: I built a multiplayer Wordle where you win real SOL

Privacy is the ultimate luxury in the age of AI. When it comes to health data, the stakes are even higher. Users are increasingly wary of sending sensitive symptoms to a remote server. This is where Edge AI and In-browser inference change the game. By leveraging WebGPU and Transformer models, we can build a medical symptom checker that runs entirely on the user's hardware—meaning zero server costs for you and total privacy for them.

We will focus on creating a high-performance, privacy-first AI solution that bypasses the cloud entirely. If you've been looking for a way to implement On-device LLMs using TypeScript, you're in the right place.…

Introduction to AfterLive


As developers, we often focus on building solutions for the present, but what about the future? What about the people we leave behind? I recently lost a close family member, and the experience made me realize how fragile our legacies can be. I wanted to find a way to preserve their memory, their stories, and their voice.
